# Template: Tower Defense (isometric)

Status: planned. Milestone: M4 template wave. Dimension: 2.5D (a 3D world seen through a fixed isometric camera).
Default look: `meadow`. Players: 1 to 4 co-op. Difficulty: intermediate. Conventions and API group ids:
`docs/templates/README.md`.

Sample world: **Gatekeep**. Enemies march from a portal along a winding road to your core. Place towers beside the
road, upgrade them, survive 20 waves with bosses on waves 10 and 20.

## Why this template

Tower defense is a long-running Roblox genre (judgment: no tower defense game was in the October 2026 snapshot) and a
strategy game is in Fortnite's top 20 (research doc, section 2). It
is also the catalog's "in-between" template: a 3D world with an isometric camera, so a creator sees that Metallic's
3D tools make 2.5D games with no extra API. It teaches data-driven design (waves and towers are tables), targeting,
an economy with choices, and how to show hundreds of moving enemies without sending hundreds of positions a frame.

## Game loop

1. Start with `StartingCoins`. Ten seconds before wave 1 (or press **Start wave**).
2. Click a free tile beside the road, pick a tower. A ghost shows its range ring.
3. Enemies walk the road. Towers fire automatically. Kills pay coins to every player.
4. Between waves: upgrade (3 levels per tower), change targeting (First, Strongest, Closest), sell for `SellRefund`.
5. An enemy reaching the core costs core health equal to its threat. Core at 0: defeat.
6. Survive `WaveCount` waves: victory. Results show waves, kills and coins.

Up to 4 players share the map and the core; each has their own coins and towers. Enemy health rises 40% per extra
player.

## Enemies and towers (defaults)

| Enemy | Speed (studs/s) | Health | Threat | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Scout | 10 | 30 | 1 | fast, fragile |
| Grunt | 6 | 100 | 2 | the baseline |
| Brute | 3.5 | 600 | 5 | armour: 5 less damage per hit |
| Swarm | 8 | 15 | 1 | comes in groups of 10 |
| Golem (boss) | 2.5 | 6,000 (wave 10), 25,000 (wave 20) | 50 | splits into 6 Scouts at half health |

| Tower | Cost | Range | Attack | Upgrades (cost: x0.75, x1.5, x3 of base) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Bolt | 100 | 18 | 12 damage, 2.5 shots/s, one target | +damage, +range, +rate |
| Mortar | 250 | 8 to 30 | 40 splash in 5 studs, 0.5 shots/s | +damage, +radius, +rate |
| Frost | 150 | 14 | slows everything in range by 40% for 1.5 s; 3 damage per pulse, 1 pulse/s | +slow, +range, +damage |
| Mint | 200 | none | +30 coins to its owner at the end of each wave | +15 coins per level |

Waves 1 to 20 are a table in `Shared.Waves`: enemy type, count, spacing and start delay per group. Waves past 20 (if
`WaveCount` is higher) are generated by a formula in the same module.

## Camera

Scriptable camera, yaw 45 degrees, pitch 35 degrees down, field of view 14 degrees from 200 to 600 studs away (a
narrow field of view from far away looks almost orthographic, with no new API). WASD or drag with the right mouse to
pan, wheel to zoom, Q and E to turn 90 degrees. Panning stops at the map edge. Gamepad: left stick pans, right stick
turns.

## Level layout

Field 160 x 160 studs at y 0 on a raised plateau with cliffs (Wedges) down to water. About 1,000 Parts.

| Feature | Where | Contents |
|---|---|---|
| Portal | (-70, 0, -70) | an arch of Parts, Look:Hazard |
| Road | 12 waypoints from portal to core | 8 studs wide, slightly sunken (y -0.2), Look:Ground in a second shade; length about 420 studs |
| Core | (70, 0, 70) | a crystal on a plinth, Look:Goal, health bar in a `BillboardGui` |
| Tiles | everywhere else on the plateau | a 4 x 4 grid of build tiles (about 900), each a thin Part tagged `Buildable` with a `TileId`; tiles touching the road are 30% darker so the best spots are visible |
| Decoration | edges | trees and rocks, not on tiles |

Enemies follow the `Waypoints` Folder only; the road Parts are only what players see. To change the route, a creator
moves waypoints and re-lays the road Parts by hand (tutorial step 4). `Shared.Path` warns in Output if a waypoint
sits on a `Buildable` tile, so a creator spots a mismatch on the next Play.

## Instances

```
Workspace
  Map (Folder): Plateau, Cliffs, Decoration (Folder)      Look role tags
  Road (Folder)                                           road Parts
  Waypoints (Folder)                                      W1 ... W12 (invisible Parts, attribute Order)
  Tiles (Folder)                                          Buildable Parts
  Portal (Model), Core (Model)
  Towers (Folder), Enemies (Folder, client-side visuals only)
ReplicatedStorage
  GameSettings (Configuration)
  Remotes (Folder)
  TowerModels (Folder): Bolt, Mortar, Frost, Mint (Model, one per level: Bolt1, Bolt2, Bolt3)
  EnemyModels (Folder): Scout, Grunt, Brute, Swarm, Golem (Model)
  Shared (Folder): Waves, Towers, Enemies, Path (ModuleScript; Path turns a distance along the road into a position)
ServerScriptService
  WaveService, EnemyService, TowerService, EconomyService, CoreService (Script)
StarterPlayer.StarterPlayerScripts
  IsoCameraController, PlacementController, EnemyViewController, TowerFxController, HudController (LocalScript)
StarterGui
  Hud (ScreenGui): Wave, CoreHealth, Coins, TowerBar (4 buttons), StartWave, SpeedToggle
  TowerPanel (ScreenGui): upgrade, sell, targeting for the selected tower
```

## How enemies stay cheap

The server owns each enemy as a record: type, health, distance along the road, slow effects. It does not create a
Part per enemy. Each Heartbeat it advances distances and runs tower targeting with `Shared.Path`. Clients get
`WaveStarted` (who spawns when), then batched `EnemySync` corrections 4 times a second (unreliable) and `EnemyDied`
events. Each client draws enemies from a pool of Models, placing them with the same `Shared.Path` maths and smoothing
toward the corrections. 200 enemies cost the network about 4 small messages a second instead of 12,000 position
updates. This is the template's main lesson and its scripts say so in their headers.

## Scripts

| Script | Side | Job |
|---|---|---|
| `WaveService` | server | Runs waves from `Shared.Waves`, the between-wave timer, vote to start early, fast forward (all players agree). `-- TRY: add a Swarm group to wave 3.` |
| `EnemyService` | server | Enemy records, movement, slows, armour, boss split, reaching the core. |
| `TowerService` | server | Place, upgrade, sell, targeting modes; each tower picks a target and fires on its own timer. `-- TRY: change Bolt's TARGET_MODE default to "Strongest".` |
| `EconomyService` | server | Per-player coins, kill rewards to all players, wave bonus, Mint income. |
| `CoreService` | server | Core health, defeat and victory, results. |
| `IsoCameraController` | client | The camera described above. |
| `PlacementController` | client | Hover a tile, ghost tower, range ring, red ghost and cross icon on bad tiles, click to place. |
| `EnemyViewController` | client | Enemy Model pool, positions from `Shared.Path`, smoothing, health bars on hover. |
| `TowerFxController` | client | Bolt tracers, mortar arcs (tweened ball), frost rings, hit flashes. |
| `HudController` | client | Wave counter, core health, coins, tower bar with hotkeys 1 to 4, tower panel. |

## RemoteEvents

| Name | Direction | Payload | Server checks |
|---|---|---|---|
| `PlaceTower` | client to server | `{tower, tileId}` | tower type exists; tile is `Buildable`, free, not on the road; enough coins; under `MaxTowersPerPlayer`; at most 5 per second |
| `UpgradeTower` | client to server | `{towerId}` | owner only; below level 3; enough coins |
| `SellTower` | client to server | `{towerId}` | owner only |
| `SetTargeting` | client to server | `{towerId, mode}` | owner only; mode in the list |
| `VoteStartWave` | client to server | none | between waves; one vote per player |
| `VoteSpeed` | client to server | `{fast}` | one vote per player; speed changes only when all agree |
| `WaveStarted` | server to all | `{wave, groups, startTime}` | n/a |
| `EnemySync` | server to all (unreliable) | packed `{id, distance, health}` list | n/a |
| `EnemyDied` | server to all | `{id, reward}` | n/a |
| `TowerFired` | server to all (unreliable) | `{towerId, targetId}` | n/a; effects only |
| `CoreDamaged` | server to all | `{health}` | n/a |
| `GameOver` | server to all | `{won, wave, kills}` | n/a |

## UI

Top left: `Wave 7 / 20` and the next wave's enemy icons. Top centre: core health bar. Top right: coins. Bottom: tower
bar with cost under each icon and hotkeys. Selecting a tower opens a side panel: level pips, upgrade cost, sell value,
targeting mode. Range rings and tile highlights use shapes and outlines as well as colour.

## Game settings

| Attribute | Default | Range | Effect |
|---|---|---|---|
| `StartingCoins` | 300 | 0 to 5,000 | Coins at the start |
| `CoreHealth` | 100 | 10 to 1,000 | Core health |
| `WaveCount` | 20 | 5 to 50 | Waves to win |
| `EnemyHealthScale` | 1.0 | 0.25 to 5 | Enemy health multiplier |
| `EnemySpeedScale` | 1.0 | 0.5 to 2 | Enemy speed multiplier |
| `KillRewardScale` | 1.0 | 0.25 to 5 | Coins per kill multiplier |
| `WaveBonus` | 50 | 0 to 500 | Coins per player after each wave |
| `SellRefund` | 0.7 | 0 to 1 | Share of spent coins returned on sell |
| `TimeBetweenWaves` | 15 | 0 to 60 | Seconds before the next wave starts by itself |
| `MaxTowersPerPlayer` | 30 | 5 to 100 | Tower limit per player |
| `AllowFastForward` | true | bool | Allow 2x speed when all players agree |
| `ExtraPlayerHealth` | 0.4 | 0 to 1 | Enemy health added per extra player |

## Multiplayer

Shared core, per-player coins and towers; only a tower's owner can upgrade or sell it. Late joiners get the current
wave, every tower and a full enemy sync, plus `StartingCoins` scaled to the current wave. A player who leaves has their
towers sold to the remaining players' shared refund (split evenly), so the defence does not vanish silently.

## Tutorial

1. "Press Play. Place two Bolt towers by the road and beat wave 1." (`remote_fired` WaveStarted for wave 2)
2. "Try the Frost look for a winter map." (`look_applied`)
3. "In Game settings, set Starting coins to 1000. Play again." (`setting_changed` StartingCoins)
4. "Change the road: move Waypoints.W6 somewhere else and re-lay those road Parts." (`property_changed` W6 Position)
5. "Open Shared.Waves. Follow the TRY line to add a Swarm group to wave 3." (`script_edited` Waves)
6. "Play to wave 5." (`remote_fired` WaveStarted for wave 5)
7. "Name your defence game and share it." (`renamed_game`)

## Style variants

`meadow` (default). `frost`: snow plateau, ice road. `dusk`: canyon at sunset. `noir`: night defence where towers carry
`PointLight`s. Swap-in art: any Model named like the ones in `TowerModels` or `EnemyModels`. Camera variant: set the
pitch to 90 degrees in `IsoCameraController` for a straight top-down game.

## New API this template needs

A1 (`Waves`, `Towers`, `Enemies`, `Path`), A2, A3, A4, A5 (`TweenService`, `UserInputService`), **A6 (CFrame)**, A7
(`Raycast` for tile picking), A8, A12, A14, **A16 (`UnreliableRemoteEvent`, `GetServerTimeNow`)**, **A19 (scriptable
camera, `FieldOfView`, `ViewportPointToRay`)**, A20 (pan, zoom, turn keys; touch drag later), A21 (`TextButton`,
`ImageButton`, `BillboardGui`), A24.

## Acceptance checks

- [ ] `tests/smoke.mscene` with 2 bots and `EnemySpeedScale` 2: bot A places 3 Bolts, bot B places a Frost; a Bolt
      placed on the road and on an occupied tile are refused; B tries to sell A's tower (refused); wave 1 clears with
      no core damage; A upgrades a Bolt to level 3 and sells it (coins back = 70% of spent); with `CoreHealth` 1 and no
      towers on wave 2, `GameOver{won = false}` fires once. Print `TD_SMOKE_OK`.
- [ ] 200 enemies on screen with 30 towers: 60 fps on the reference PC; server sends at most 8 `EnemySync` messages
      per second.
- [ ] Two clients show the same enemy within 1 stud of each other at the same server time.
- [ ] A full 20-wave run with a scripted build order is winnable at default settings and lost with no towers.
- [ ] Screenshots in `meadow`, `frost`, `dusk`, `noir`.
